title: Meet the National Employment Standards and award terms
what: Give employees at least the National Employment Standards and the terms of any modern award that covers them.

sources.title: Fair Work Act 2009
sources.quote: An employer must not contravene a provision of the National Employment Standards.

sources.title: Fair Work Act 2009
sources.quote: A person must not contravene a term of a modern award.

reach.note: Companies that are constitutional (trading or financial) corporations, in every state and territory.

sources.title: Fair Work Act 2009
sources.quote: A national system employer is: (a) a constitutional corporation, so far as it employs, or usually employs, an individual;

reach.note: Unincorporated employers are in the national system in the states that referred their powers and in the territories; in WA they are in the state system.

sources.title: Which system of employment laws applies
sources.publisher: Government of Western Australia (Private Sector Labour Relations)
sources.quote: The state system covers: Private sector businesses and their employees that operate as: Sole traders. Partnerships, where none of the partners in the business is a constitutional corporation (trading or financial corporation).

confidence_note: Which award applies depends on the industry and the work; awards are not yet linked to classes. The Fair Work Ombudsman is not yet in bodies.json.

assessment.summary: Every employer must meet the National Employment Standards and any award or agreement that covers its staff.

marks.reason: Working out which award applies and meeting its terms adds compliance complexity for every employer.

assessment.confidence_note: Economic reasoning and desk research only; no evaluation of this requirement found. Drafted 7 Nov 2026, not yet checked by a person.
